surface.name: Regolith
surface.summary: The loose top layer of broken rock and dust, ground up by billions of years of small impacts. It is only a few metres thick in most places.

surface.name: Megaregolith
surface.summary: The deeper, coarser layer of fractured rock below the regolith, broken up by the largest ancient impacts. It can be kilometres thick.

terrains.name: Highlands
terrains.summary: The bright, heavily cratered highlands are the Moon's original crust: light-coloured anorthosite rock, rich in calcium and aluminium, that floated to the top of the early magma ocean about 4.15–4.4 billion years ago.

terrains.name: Maria
terrains.summary: The dark maria are plains of basalt lava, rich in iron and titanium, that flooded low basins about 3.0–3.5 billion years ago. They look smooth and dark because the lava filled in the older craters.
